business_scope.primary_industry_name: Financial Market News Aggregation and Syndication Feed

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law heritage with customary-law overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa - New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (in force)
Samoa - Australia Tax Information Exchange Agreement (in force)
Samoa - New Zealand Tax Information Exchange Agreement (in force)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus, regional FTA in force for Samoa since 13 December 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2019 and 2020), ss. 28, 29, 102A and Schedule 7; International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2019/2021; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2000 (as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2014 (as amended); SIFA AML/CFT Administrative Guidelines (as updated 2022) imposing UBO record-keeping and reporting duties on licensed registered agents.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: the beneficial-ownership register is maintained by the licensed registered agent at the statutory registered office in Apia; full legal access is granted to the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), the Samoan Financial Intelligence Unit, and domestic law-enforcement/regulatory authorities upon lawful request; no public inspection of the IC UBO register is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each UBO, director, and qualifying shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (for Convention-source documents) or Consular Legalization at the Samoan High Commission/Consulate for non-Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-applicable-funds letter for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated home-jurisdiction bank of the beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille / consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or certified equivalent) for any corporate shareholder
Memory and Articles of Association / Charter of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder acting through its authorized officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy with notarization and Apostille / consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO and director declaration (SIFA IC-UBO form)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each UBO, director, and authorized signatory executed before the Samoan licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registered-agent attested declaration (retained for SIFA/law-enforcement inspection; Apostille not required for internal statutory register but recommended for onward banking)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, Samoa domestic sanctions/designation register, and EU/UK consolidated lists; PEPs, family members, and close associates are treated as enhanced-risk, requiring independent source-of-wealth evidence and senior compliance-committee approval before engagement; screening is re-run within 24 hours of any sanctions-list update; a FATF-compliant risk-based approach applies to the low-risk newswire business model.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - International Companies Registry; name-clearance applications are submitted exclusively through SIFA-licensed registered agents; there is no public self-service portal for IC name reservations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in English characters; a dual Chinese company name (中文名称) may be recorded in the charter and UBO file as a translation, with the English name prevailing in any conflict; the name must be distinctive and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name in the SIFA IC register or to a domestic name reserved at the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Companies Registry; no phonetic transliteration certification is required for the registered English name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, SIFA issues a written refusal notice to the registered agent within 5 business days; the applicant may (i) file a formal written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days, attaching a negative name-search report and written arguments on distinctiveness, or (ii) immediately resubmit an amended name under a fresh reservation window; the Registrar determines the appeal within 15 business days; a second refusal is final absent ministerial (Cabinet) consent or a further name amendment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible: the International Companies Act 1987 requires a statutory registered office in Samoa maintained by a licensed registered agent; the newswire company itself may operate entirely remotely, using the agent's physical Apia office as the service-of-process and records address; a bare virtual-mailbox arrangement without a licensed agent maintaining physical custody of statutory records is not compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a standard low-risk, non-banking, license-exempt newswire IC; probability rises to 20%-25% upon sanctions/PEP alerts, adverse media, or unresolved UBO red flags exceeding 10% ownership.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the SIFA Fees Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies Act 1987 and SIFA Fees Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered agent annual fee (includes UBO register maintenance and AML/CFT record custody)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent (private licenced service provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SIFA-licensed agents for low-risk standard ICs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory registered office fee (virtual office at agent's Apia address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (bundled with registered agent retainer)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of incorporation documents, UBO declarations, and passport copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark and Notaries and Public Officers tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: MFAT apostille tariff per document (approximate bundle rate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk corporate screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of charter and UBO file (English / Chinese)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per certified page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External legal consultation fee for pre-incorporation structuring
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed scope, approximately 2 hours senior counsel time)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), sections 4 (Incorporation), 7 (Memorandum and Articles), 29 (Share Capital), 42 (Directors), and 69 (Registered Agent and Office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Companies Registrar, Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: International Company Incorporation Form (Form 1) together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; share capital is fixed in the Memorandum; escrow account rules not applicable for non-financial holding entities
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription of the initial issued shares be and is hereby approved, and the subscribers be recorded in the register of members. RESOLVED that the registered office be established at the place stated in the Memorandum, and the registered agent be appointed. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed director and [Name] be appointed secretary, each to hold office subject to these Articles. RESOLVED that the directors be authorised to open bank accounts, prepare necessary filings, and take all steps required to obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and any operational permissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registrar, MCIL Companies Office, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed company names via the Companies Office e-Services portal or physically at the Registrar's counter. The names must end with 'International Limited' or 'IC' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. Include a brief description of the syndicated finance newswire business to facilitate availability review. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain a name reservation certificate valid for 30 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the applicant may file a written objection with the Registrar within 14 days; alternatively, submit a revised name list and pay an additional reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Lawyer or licensed company formation agent; filing to be made with the Samoa International Companies Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association using the standard International Company template, adapted to permit tax-exempt status and restricted activity under the International Companies Act. Have the first subscriber execute the documents in the presence of a witness, and arrange notarization of signatures if required by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (duly executed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If constitutional documents contain defective attestation or missing mandatory clauses, the Registrar will issue a query memo; counsel must amend and re-submit within 15 business days to avoid abandonment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registrar, Companies Office, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 together with the executed constitutional documents and the name reservation certificate through the Companies Office e-Services portal. Pay the official state filing fee of USD 200 (or equivalent in WST Tala) via bank transfer or the MCIL cashier. Verify that the receipt is generated and retained for certificate issuance.
required_dossiers: Consents of first director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for incomplete documentation, the Registrar issues a deficiency notice identifying the missing items; the applicant has 10 business days to cure the defect without penalty. Re-submission after the cure period requires a fresh application and fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review of Form 1 and supporting documents, the Registrar will enter the company in the International Companies Register and issue the Certificate of Incorporation. Verify that the certificate states the company name, incorporation date, and company number. Download the certified copy from the portal or collect the physical certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued within the service level, the applicant may submit a written expedite request to the Registrar; any error in the certificate may be rectified by filing a Notice of Correction with supporting evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must maintain a licensed registered agent and a registered office in Samoa at all times. Confirm the agent has accepted appointment in writing, and file the Notice of Change of Registered Office/Agent with the Registrar if the details differ from those in Form 1. Obtain the agent's physical address and register it as the official service address.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent/lease or service agreement
Notice of Registered Office/Agent (Form 4, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to maintain a registered agent leads to administrative strike-off; remedy is to re-appoint a licensed agent and file a restoration application with late fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company secretary under supervision of the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause the company secretary to prepare and maintain the register of members, register of directors and secretaries, and register of charges. Issue share certificates to the initial subscribers and, if adopted, procure a common seal. Retain all records at the registered office as required by sections 71 and 76 of the International Companies Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar finds missing statutory records during inspection, the company must compile the registers retrospectively and file a declaration of rectification; penalties may apply for failure to maintain records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Business Registration Endorsements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Revenue (MOR) and Samoa International Companies Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Ministry of Revenue for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for administrative purposes. Since the International Company is tax-exempt on foreign-source income and qualifies for the International Companies Act exemption, submit the Certificate of Incorporation and a declaration of exempt activity. For the financial newswire feed, register with the Samoa Companies Office as a non-financial business entity to facilitate banking onboarding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TIN application is delayed due to proof of identity issues, provide a certified copy of the director's passport and a bank reference; appeal through the Ministry of Revenue's taxpayer services unit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a syndicated finance newswire service; no manufacturing or industrial activity is undertaken. The relevant registration is with the Samoa International Companies Registrar.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; the company may commence financial news aggregation and wire services upon incorporation and registration with the Ministry of Revenue for tax status.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity is an information service with no physical infrastructure, no discharge, and no land disturbance; no EIA or environmental permit is required under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The company must nevertheless comply with general waste disposal rules and any server equipment noise or electronic waste handling requirements under Samoa's environment regulations, if an office is leased.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a pure digital service; if a physical office is established in Samoa, a fire safety clearance from the Fire and Emergency Services Authority and a building occupancy certificate from the Lands and Titles Court or relevant municipal authority are recommended but not a precondition for incorporation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry for Revenue; taxpayer portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws; offshore entity registrar: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), https://www.sifa.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned entity must first incorporate as an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 through a licensed offshore service provider; the IC files its charter with the Registrar under SIFA/MCIL, then applies to the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) for a Tax Identification Number (TIN). Compulsory VAGST registration applies only where taxable supplies in Samoa exceed WST 100,000 annual turnover; a pure offshore IC deriving exclusively foreign-source income ordinarily obtains a TIN as a tax-exempt registrant without VAGST registration, for banking and AML compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Statutorily exempt International Company under the International Companies Act 1987; offshore-source income, distributions and capital gains exempt from Samoa income tax and withholding tax; subject only to annual government licence fees)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Samoa ICs are statutorily tax-exempt regardless of ownership or management location. Elections available: (i) IC status election under International Companies Act 1987; (ii) VAGST cash-basis or simplified accounting election for qualifying small suppliers; (iii) treaty tie-breaker and hybrid mismatch adjustments under Samoa's double tax agreements and OECD/G20 BEPS Inclusive Framework commitments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the VAGST Act 2004
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual taxable turnover (approx. USD 37,000); compulsory registration for persons making taxable supplies in Samoa above the threshold; offshore ICs supplying only exempt or exported services remain registrable on an optional basis
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing mandate currently applies in Samoa. The SRA requires standard tax invoices, an electronic VAGST return filed via the SRA online portal, and retention of underlying records; government-approved real-time clearance e-invoicing has not been enacted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to physical exports of goods, international transport, and specified exported services supplied to non-resident recipients for use wholly outside Samoa. The syndicated finance newswire/API subscription feed qualifies as an exported service where the subscriber is a non-resident financial institution and the service benefit is wholly consumed offshore; evidence of delivery, payment and foreign use must be retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CusDec) evidencing physical export and customs clearance
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / electronic delivery log for cross-border goods or service transmission
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) from a licensed Samoa commercial bank evidencing receipt of export consideration in convertible foreign currency
Export service contract and API delivery logs demonstrating delivery of the syndicated finance newswire feed to non-resident subscribers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger retrospective clawback of input VAGST credits, penalties up to 150% of the tax evaded, monetary fines up to WST 100,000 per offence, and/or imprisonment under the VAGST Act 2004 and Tax Administration Act 2012; SRA audit may re-characterise zero-rating where the non-resident recipient, place of supply, or economic substance tests are not satisfied.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), acting as the foreign exchange administration under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1977 (as amended).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is not freely convertible offshore. Current-account payments and profit remittances are generally approved upon submission of documentary evidence through an authorized dealer (licensed commercial bank). Capital-account transactions, including inbound debt/equity transfers and outward investment, are subject to prior CBS approval unless the entity is a non-resident International Company (IC). An IC registered under the International Companies Act 1987 operates as a tax-exempt non-resident enterprise, may maintain fully foreign-currency-denominated accounts, and may remit profits/dividends offshore without local withholding or exchange-control approval, provided no Samoan-source income is derived and the company remains in good standing with the Registrar of International Companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident exporters, proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa through an authorized dealer within 180 days of the date of export; 100% of the export receipts in foreign currency must be surrendered to the dealer in exchange for WST within 30 days of receipt, unless CBS has granted a specific retention allowance or exemption. For a non-resident International Company, the surrender obligation is not triggered because the IC is outside the exchange-control 'specified person' classification and cannot conduct business with Samoan residents; all export-derived foreign currency from non-resident counterparties is held freely in designated offshore accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Multi-Currency Account / Trade Finance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for domestic WST clearing and regulated payments; Medium only as a supplementary non-WST routing channel. Samoa does not currently maintain a licensed EMI category, and any entity holding WST deposits or issuing local-currency payment instruments is required to hold a banking licence under the Financial Institutions Act 2016. Offshore digital EMIs cannot be direct participants in Samoa Interchange Settlement (SIS) or CBS clearing infrastructure; they may be used solely for receiving and disbursing USD/EUR/GBP proceeds through a correspondent bank, provided the EMI does not solicit Samoan-resident clients and all sampled funds are transmitted to a licensed Samoan bank for domestic conversion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner (or an authorized professional introducer) is generally required for first-time account opening. Remote opening may be permitted in strictly limited circumstances where the bank adopts CBS AML/CFT remote due diligence protocols, performs a live video interview with compliance management, and receives a banker's 'reasonable assurance' letter from the foreign introducer. In practice, Samoan banks prefer an in-person appearance at the branch or a board-authorized local agent who executes the account mandate before attested witnesses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company with zero active income opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing; International Company Certificate of Incorporation; constitutive documents with ownership chain; board resolution authorizing account opening and expenditure purpose; formal legal opinion confirming waiver or tax-exempt status; source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, audit reports); detailed business plan and non-domiciliary declaration; AML/CFT self-assessment risk register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Financial-news and syndicated-fastwire activity subjected to money-value-transmitter classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Samoan counsel confirming ISIC 6391 / NAICS 519110 is a publishing and newswire aggregation activity, not a deposit-taking, investment, remittance, or money-service business; contractual service agreement showing only distribution of data and analysis without dealing in securities; customer-side KYC downloads; demonstration that no client funds are held or routed through the IC accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or opaque beneficial-ownership jurisdiction exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copy and notarized utility bill; source-of-wealth report from the upstream professional intermediary; certified copy of the corporate register extract in the ultimate-parent jurisdiction; full ownership chain to final natural persons; sanctions/PEP screening results and negative press search output; external legal counsel indemnity or comfort letter covering beneficial-owner identification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loan transfers are routed via SWIFT MT103 with Samoan beneficiary bank BIC and purpose code IRU / capital injection code applicable to ICs. Funds are credited to the IC's dedicated Capital Escrow Account (Bank of Samoa or ANZ) after the bank matches the remitter to the registered shareholder, runs sanctions screening, and files a CBS cross-border reporting form. A supporting board resolution, share certificate, and remittance advice stating 'Equity Investment' or 'Shareholder Loan' are mandatory. For non-resident ICs, prior CBS exchange-control approval is not required, but IRS/CRS self-certification and a UBO declaration are required at onboarding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are made using SWIFT MT103 for electronic cash transfers against invoices, SWIFT MT700 for documentary letter-of-credit issuance, MT707 for amendments, MT710/730/750 for documentary advice, and MT760 for standby guarantee obligations. USD leg settles via Fedwire/CHIPS between correspondent banks; WST leg settles via the CBS clearing house or Samoa Interchange Settlement (SIS). All outgoing disbursements must be matched to a board-approved weekly Treasury Payment Schedule and to the original invoice/contract repository; tax clearance certification is required for any WST payment to a Samoan resident beneficiary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore WST/USD plain-vanilla forwards (up to 12 months) executed through a CBS-authorized dealer with documented commercial need
Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) on WST/USD with a non-Samoan bank, limited to hedging projected newswire subscription revenues overseas
USD/WST cross-currency swaps for matching foreign-currency liquidity and offshore dividend timing
Plain-vanilla FX options on USD/GBP/EUR/AUD for anticipated syndicated-finance transaction settlement
Natural hedging via multi-currency accounts held in USD, EUR, GBP, AUD and NZD to minimize the need for FX conversion
Correspondent-backed reimbursements using SWIFT MT202 for interbank funding purposes only

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company annual return and annual government fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies, submitted through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of incorporation; the licensed registered agent must file the annual return within 30 days after the anniversary date and the annual government fee is due by the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues penalties under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations; failure to pay annual fees for more than six months after the anniversary renders the International Company liable to administrative strike-off by the Registrar and loss of the benefits of separate legal personality.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to a standard, non-licensed Samoa International Company; the Registrar may impose an audit requirement by specific direction, and an audit would be mandatory only if the company obtains an applicable Samoa financial services license.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting records must fairly reflect the company's transactions and financial position under the International Companies Act 2012; statutory financial statements are not filed, but any voluntarily prepared financial statements should follow IFRS or an equivalent acceptable accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent must maintain a beneficial ownership register and obtain an annual confirmation from the International Company identifying all shareholders and beneficial owners; any share transfer must be approved and entered in the Register of Members, with the registered agent updating the UBO register and including the transfer in the annual confirmation filed with the Registrar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000–US$7,500 (voluntary certified audit; no statutory audit required)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying International Companies (ICs) under the International Companies Act 1987 are exempt from income tax pursuant to the Income Tax Act 2012 exemption certificate regime; effective rate is 0% on foreign-source syndicated financial newswire revenue. Exemption requires an SIFSA-registered license, a licensed resident agent in Samoa, a registered office in Apia, no Samoan-resident trading, and no Samoa-source revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR2 (Income Tax Return for Companies); filed electronically via the Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MfR) e-Tax portal or by paper submission to the MfR Apia office
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed on or before the last day of the third month following the end of the year of income; for a 31 December year-end the due date is 31 March. Provisional tax is payable in quarterly instalments during the year of income as prescribed by the MfR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, Tax File Number (TFN/IRD number), registered office in Samoa, and licensed agent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SIFSA-licensed resident agent's Samoa address; the beneficial owner's foreign address should not be used as the registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting period covered by the return (standard 12-month period ending 31 December)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs may request a substituted accounting period with MfR approval; without approval the calendar year applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income derived from all activities, including syndicated financial news feed subscription revenue, API fees, and data licensing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude Samoa-source income; revenue settled via Swift Wire, and card/PayFac settlement via Stripe, is foreign-source when the subscribers are non-residents and the contracts are concluded outside Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income exempt under the International Companies Act 1987 exemption certificate and applicable double tax agreements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the exemption certificate reference; global financial market news aggregation revenue qualifies as exempt foreign-source income if no Samoan sales activity occurs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable business expenses: editorial licensing, market data costs, API hosting, bandwidth, cloud infrastructure, and personnel
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be evidenced by supplier invoices and priced at arm's length; related-party charges are scrutinized under the transfer pricing provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 27% less foreign tax credits and available offsets; exempt ICs will compute zero
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A zero amount is appropriate only while the IC exemption certificate is current; any inadvertent Samoa-source revenue must be declared and taxed at 27%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: the greater of WST 100 or 25% of the tax payable; late payment: a surcharge of 1% per month on the unpaid amount; incorrect returns: penalty of 20% of the tax shortfall; fraudulent or wilfully misleading returns: penalty up to 100% of the shortfall and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Samoa does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, including dividends paid out of exempt International Company profits
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's DTA network is limited (New Zealand and Australia are the principal partners). To invoke treaty relief: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the beneficial owner's residence jurisdiction; (2) submit to the MfR a Treaty Relief Application together with the TRC, the underlying contract (loan, licence, or supply agreement), and a beneficial ownership declaration; (3) the MfR endorses the applicable reduced rate, which the Samoan paying agent then applies. The TRC must be current, officially certified, and dated within 12 months; the recipient must include the income in its home-country tax return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 10% on payments to non-residents; royalties 15% on payments to non-residents. Treaty relief: the New Zealand and Australia DTAs may reduce royalty withholding to 5% (subject to beneficial ownership and substance); interest remains at 10% under the treaties. Dividend withholding is 0% domestically and is not increased by treaty application.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory de minimis threshold is codified in Samoa's Income Tax Act 2012. Prudent compliance practice: maintain a contemporaneous Local File where annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed WST 1,000,000, and a Master File where group-wide turnover exceeds WST 5,000,000; the MfR retains the right to require documentation at lower values where evasion indicators exist.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) modelled on BVI or Isle of Man. However, the 0% IC regime and treaty access require demonstrable substance: a SIFSA-licensed agent, a physical registered office in Samoa, board minutes adopted in Samoa, a Samoan bank account, and substantive offshore management control over the syndicated finance feed. The General Anti-Avoidance Rule in the Tax Administration Act 2012 permits the MfR to disregard any entity or transaction lacking economic substance and to re-characterize a bare shell as taxable in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting foreign-source syndicated news revenue from the return, falsifying the exempt status, or knowingly under-declaring taxable income to the MfR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Evasion penalty of up to 100% of the tax shortfall (minimum WST 5,000), additional fines of up to WST 50,000, and imprisonment for up to 5 years under the Tax Administration Act 2012; confiscation of evaded amounts plus monthly interest surcharges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the filing of false returns are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the shortfall; the Commissioner may issue travel bans preventing departure from Samoa until all outstanding tax liabilities are secured or satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abuse of IC Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Trading with Samoan residents, deriving Samoa-source subscription revenue, failing to maintain a SIFSA-licensed agent and registered office, or failing to pay the annual government fee (USD 500-2,000 depending on share capital)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Forfeiture of the International Company tax exemption; retroactive taxation at 27% on all income derived from the date of offending activity; back-payment of the annual government fee with monthly penalties; and possible strike-off of the company registration under the International Companies Act 1987
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the IC is found to be a sham or façade; directors become personally liable for unpaid company taxes and creditor claims; restraint orders, travel bans, and disqualification from managing any Samoa-registered company apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing the true beneficial owners, failing to maintain a register of members and beneficial owners, or failing to report suspicious transactions related to the financial newswire subscription payments under the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2021
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines up to WST 500,000 and officer fines up to WST 100,000; forfeiture of the proceeds of crime; deregistration of the International Company; adverse regulatory findings recorded by SIFSA and the Central Bank of Samoa
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal criminal liability with imprisonment up to 14 years, personal asset freezing orders, confiscation of interests, and statutory travel bans pending the conclusion of AML investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing related foreign affiliates non-arm's length prices for the financial data feed, excessive royalty or mark-up inflation, or structuring intercompany payments to erode taxable profits in a jurisdiction where tax is due
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Commissioner's transfer pricing adjustment under the Income Tax Act 2012, an accuracy penalty of 20% of the adjustment amount, plus monthly interest at 1% on the underpaid tax; repeat offenses escalate to the 100% evasion penalty
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in or approve sham pricing arrangements are jointly and severally liable for the diverted profits and civil restitution; serious cases trigger non-resident director travel bans and contempt of court sanctions.
